subject: Onboarding sprint: GPU pool topology, burst SLAs, and regional preference
messages:
From: Judy Lee <judy.lee@orion.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@orion.ai
Date: 2026-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated GPU onboarding — initial scoping and timeline

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Per our conversation, Orion is ready to move from pilot to a dedicated GPU pool for our inference stack. Wed like to confirm a few items so engineering and procurement can align: 

- Preferred region: eu-west-1 (data residency preference)
- Expected steady-state QPS: ~1200 requests/min (avg payloads ~300 tokens)
- Burst tolerance: up to 4x steady-state during batch windows (midnight UTC)
- SLA ask: 99.9% monthly uptime and 150ms p50 on 8k token tail requests if possible

Attached is a scoping worksheet with sample traffic patterns and a draft SOW placeholder (orion-scoping-sheet.xlsx). Can we schedule a 30-minute kickoff to lock topology (single-region vs multi-region), autoscale policy, and procurement milestones?

Procurement wants any reserved capacity pricing and expected billing cadence before their internal 10/10 review.

Thanks — looking to get the mutual action plan started.

Best,
Judy Lee
Head of Platform
Orion AI

<Attachment: orion-scoping-sheet.xlsx (xlsx)>
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Judy Lee <judy.lee@orion.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T10:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU onboarding — initial scoping and timeline

Judy, thanks — this is a great starting point.

I can run the kickoff with engineering and CS tomorrow at 10am PT / 18:00 CET if that works for your team. High level thoughts ahead of the call so we can be efficient:

1) Region: eu-west-1 is fine; recommend single-primary with warm-standby in eu-central for failover (adds modest cross-region cost but preserves data residency for read/write).
2) Topology options (we'll pick on the call):
   - Single pool (8xA100 equivalent) with multi-slot autoscale for steady + burst.
   - Multi-pool split (inference-optimized v. batch/priming) to isolate low-latency requests from large batch priming.
3) Autoscale / burst policy suggestions:
   - Steady target concurrency tuned to 1.2x observed average token throughput.
   - Burst buffer: allow 3-4x short-duration burst via reserved burst capacity + on-demand spillover to a lower-cost variant (quantized model) with automatic fallback.
4) SLA feasibility: 99.9% is achievable; p50 150ms on long-tail depends on model variant and batching — we'll measure during activation.

Ask for the kickoff: can you confirm the two busiest daily windows in UTC and whether priming traffic is batched or ad-hoc? That determines whether we recommend separate batch pool.

I'll attach a short kickoff agenda and a draft mutual action plan to the Drive link and bring the ops playbook.

— Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Customer Engineering, Redwood Inference
https://drive.redwood.com/shared/orion/onboard-kickoff

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Judy Lee <judy.lee@orion.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T13:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU onboarding — initial scoping and timeline

Judy / team — quick technical notes to have on the call so we don't get stuck on the basics: 

- Pool sizing: with 1200 req/min and avg 300 tokens, rough token rate puts steady GPU utilization at ~40-55% on an 8xA100-equivalent pool if using int8 quantized runtime for batch jobs; unquantized p50 latency will be higher.
- Burst: we can provision a "burst bucket" of reserved instances sized for 3x steady for 5-10 minute bursts; beyond that we recommend fallback to a quantized variant or preemptible capacity.
- Autoscale knobs we will propose:
  * target_utilization: 0.6 (scale out when sustained over 60s)
  * max_scale_factor: 4.0 (pre-agreed cap for cost control)
  * cooldown: 120s for scale down to prevent thrash
- KV/cache priming: if you have repeat prefixes, enabling prefix caching will reduce tail latency; please flag top 50 prefixes in the sheet.
- Model pinning & versions: recommend pinning to a production hash for the first 30 days; rollout a canary with 5% traffic for any model change.

I'll bring a short config template to the kickoff that maps these knobs to Redwood's Console options.

Karthik
Staff Inference Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Judy Lee <judy.lee@orion.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU onboarding — initial scoping and timeline

Judy — looping in CS and procurement steps so timelines are aligned. A few operational checkpoints: 

- SOW & billing: please confirm the billing entity and PO cadence. Weve attached the draft SOW (Orion-SOW-v1.pdf) to the Drive link; procurement mentioned they expect a two-week review.
- Activation milestones (proposed):
   1) Contract & PO signed (T+0)
   2) Topology lock + region confirmation (T+3 business days)
   3) Provision pool & baseline tests (T+7)
   4) Canary traffic & latency QA (T+10)
   5) Go-live & operational handover (T+14)
- Ops runbooks: we'll assign a turn-up engineer and schedule a 2-hour dry-run for failover and autoscale stress testing.

Action items for Orion: please upload the signed SOW (or DocuSign link), confirm PO timeline, and add the top prefixes for cache priming into the scoping sheet.

Thanks — Monica Patel
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

<Attachment: Orion-SOW-v1.pdf (pdf)>
From: Judy Lee <judy.lee@orion.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@orion.ai
Date: 2026-10-02T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU onboarding — initial scoping and timeline

Thanks, team — confirming the kickoff at the time you suggested. A few quick clarifications after reviewing the notes: 

- Peak windows: 02:00-03:00 UTC (daily batch priming) and 16:00-17:00 UTC (user surge). Both are short (5-12 minutes) but intensive.
- Priming: batch priming is scheduled and will be large, we'll mark that traffic as batch in the scoping sheet.
- Procurement: PO will target a 10/12 internal approval date; we expect to sign the SOW by 10/08. Ive routed the SOW to DocuSign and shared the link here: https://docusign.com/ORION/12345 (signed)

We prefer eu-west-1 as primary; warm-standby in eu-central is fine. Agree on a 3x burst bucket capped at 4x via policy.

Uploading the filled scoping sheet with prefixes and sample payloads now. Looking forward to the kickoff.

Best,
Judy
